crossing_on_horseback.text: You ride across the valley at full speed. Behind you, Regalus—the bandit leader, the criminal who almost took your life and your medallion, the only remnant of your forgotten past—keeps snoring peacefully despite the jolts of the road. After several hours on horseback, you finally reach Kelia's Crossing, a small elven town ringed by immense fortifications, almost cut off from the rest of the world.

"Halt!" one of the elven legionaries at the gate barks. "No one enters the city without a pass; orders from the Dumvir." Eden flashes a mocking smile and simply nods toward the criminal tied to the back of his horse.

"Regalus!" the legionary exclaims. "Enter, the Dumvir will want to reward you personally. But know this: all entries and exits are forbidden from dusk onward." You follow Eden inside. The heavy city gates close behind you with a dull thud.

The streets are overflowing with people. You cut on foot through the central square, monopolized today by a gigantic market. Merchants and locals crowd the stalls, haggling loudly over all manner of goods. The sheer mass of bodies and voices creates a deafening, chaotic cacophony.

Inside the Curia, the political heart of the city, a scribe announces your arrival to the Dumvir, the town leader.

The Dumvir, bent over his work, stops when he sees Regalus. The criminal, now awake, growls and struggles against his gag.

"That scoundrel Regalus, finally apprehended!" the Dumvir rejoices. With a snap of his fingers, he has a hefty purse dropped into Eden's hand. "To whom do I have the honor of paying this bounty?" The hunter introduces himself with his usual nonchalance, then turns toward you.

"A pleasure to meet you!" the politician replies, gripping your hand firmly. He signals two legionaries to escort Regalus to his cell, then immediately stops them midmotion.

"A criminal like Regalus implies a long, tedious trial," he sighs, pinching the bridge of his nose. "I do not have time for that, especially right now..."

He then turns toward Eden.

"Double the bounty and you've got a deal," he says.

"I'm afraid that's not in the budget," the Dumvir answers, his gaze now shifting to you. "And your colleague? Would they be willing to rid Li'ark of a harmful criminal like Regalus?"

Piercing their rotten flesh with arrows is a pointless endeavor—they multiply and return in even greater numbers."
 You notice the goosebumps on his skin as flashes of those nights start crawling back in the Dumvir's head.

"We believe the surge of undead originates here, in the Crypt of the Ancients. Some ancient, forbidden magic is at work, and a necromancer of the worst kind must be behind it. I have sent my legionaries to assault the crypt time and again, but the coward hides behind an army of corpses."

remembering_how_to_fight.text: This turn of events unlocks another part of your old self. A sudden wave of forgotten knowledge floods your mind. You have been in situations like this before—more than once. And you fought. That's it: you remember how to fight! The dwarf hefts a table as if it weighs nothing and hurls it at the cuckold's two companions. Eden grabs a nearby pint, downs it in one gulp, then charges the cuckold head-on. The assassin weaves through the chaos, retrieves his blade from the floor, and blocks every way out. He has no intention of letting you leave alive.

choices.text: [START COMBAT]
Punch
Fireball

assassin_lunges_at_you.text: You send the assassin sprawling with a final punch. Nearby, the dwarf slams one elf’s head into the floor, then hurls the second straight at you. You narrowly dodge—Eden does the same. The cuckold, slower to react, takes the impact full on. At that moment, the assassin regains his senses and makes a desperate charge, blade aimed at your chest. You have no time to dodge. You're done for...

choices.text: [CONTINUE]

bard_save.text: But his blade never reaches you: the assassin is struck full force by a lightning spell. You turn around  to see the young bard, who's using her lute as a magical focus. With a single chord, she casts another spell—a sleep enchantment that hypnotizes the three elves and stops them cold. Wounded and cornered, the assassin flees. The fight is over. An uneasy silence falls over the tavern, all eyes fixed on you, waiting for your reaction.

fight_over_apologies.text: Your apologies are accepted, but they leave many disappointed. The patrons, fired up by the sudden brawl, expected a more victorious display. Eden struggles to his feet and runs his tongue over his split lips. He turns to thank the young bard, but she ignores him and returns to the stage. The tavern’s revelry resumes as if the fight were a mere interlude. Eden shrugs and invites you outside.

choices.text: Follow the hunter outside.

fight_over_silent.text: You lower your head, visibly embarrassed. Your intent may be honorable, but the patrons read it as weakness and scorn you in silence. Eden gets up with effort, licks his split lips, and tries to thank the bard, who ignores him and resumes playing. The tavern’s flow returns. Eden shrugs and asks you to follow him outside.

choices.text: Follow the hunter outside.

fight_over_provoke.text: Your threats hit home, cementing your reputation as someone not to be crossed. No patron dares meet your gaze. Eden rises with effort, passes his tongue over his split lips, and turns to thank the bard, who ignores him and resumes her tune. The tavern slips back into festivity. Eden shrugs and gestures for you to leave with him.

choices.text: Follows the hunter outside

fight_over_provoke_fail.text: Your shaky threats shatter what little charisma you earned from your victory. One patron struggles to contain his laughter. You have made a fool of yourself. Eden gets up with effort, licks his split lips, and tries to thank the bard, who ignores him and returns to the stage. The tavern moves on. Eden shrugs and invites you outside.

choices.text: Follows the hunter outside

fight_over_barbarian.text: Your rough, virile roar brings a second silence, longer than the first. Then the whole tavern joins in with a cry of victory. Glasses clink, beer spills, and one patron even buys a round. Eden rises with effort, runs his tongue over his split lips, and turns to thank the bard, who ignores him and resumes playing. The festivities roll on. Eden shrugs and asks you to step outside.

choices.text: Follows the hunter outside

fight_over_monk.text: Your unshakable calm unsettles the crowd. It is not the reaction they expected, but it earns their respect. Eden struggles to his feet, passes his tongue over his split lips, and turns to thank the bard, who ignores him and returns to her music. The tavern resumes its rhythm. Eden shrugs and invites you to go outside.

choices.text: Follows the hunter outside

eden_praises_forest_regalus_dead.text:
Outside, Eden says nothing. He studies you from head to toe, clearly unsettled by your display in the tavern, his mind racing as he pieces together a plan you will inevitably be part of.

"I misjudged you," he finally says. 

"When I met you in that web-choked forest, I took you for a helpless wimp. But after what I saw in the tavern… and the way you killed Regalus… I’m impressed. You have the makings of a true hunter."

choices.text: Tease him—is it a praise you're hearing?
Thank him politely—like you'd care about what he thinks.
Say that you took him for an arrogant asshole and you still do.
